transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because... well, I've been having to be more in front of people lately for my job, planning events and things like that. And I just can't stop staring at this one uneven-looking part of my face, especially in photos. It's really bothering me, even though everyone else tells me they barely see anything. I just... I can't ignore it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking that part of your face in mirrors or photos?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially before I have to send out event pictures or join a vendor meeting. I'll just keep checking my face in my phone camera. I end up retaking photos a bunch of times, or I try to tilt my head a certain way so it doesn't look as bad. Sometimes I'll even ask a coworker if I look weird. It just... it eats up a lot of time, honestly. Like, enough time that I can actually fall behind on my planning stuff because I'm so stuck on doing all that.
When you're around other people, are you mainly afraid that they will judge you because of that part of your face?

Um, I'm not really sure. I don't know if I'd say I'm afraid of them judging me, exactly. I just... I know it looks uneven, and it really bothers me, so I don't want people staring at it. But I haven't really thought about whether they're actually judging me as a person because of it. I just know I don't like how it looks.
Do these thoughts about that part of your face feel intrusive and unwanted to you?

Um, I'm not really sure if I'd use those exact words. I mean, I definitely wish I didn't spend so much time worrying about it, so I guess you could say it's unwanted. But I don't know if they feel... intrusive. It's more like I just know the unevenness is there, and I have to deal with it for my job. So I'm just thinking about it because I'm trying to fix how it looks for the photos or the meetings. I haven't really thought about it the way you're describing.
Have you ever avoided a social or work situation because you felt too upset about that part of your face?

No, I don't think I've ever completely avoided something. I mean... I have to be at these events and vendor meetings for my job. So even if I'm really upset about how my face looks, I still go. I might spend a ton of time stressing about it beforehand, or trying to hide it, but I haven't actually skipped work or canceled on people because of it.
Do you think that part of your face actually looks abnormal to other people?

I don't really know. I mean, I know it looks uneven to me, and it's pretty obvious when I look in the mirror. But I haven't really asked anyone else if they think it looks abnormal. I just try to cover it up or fix it so they don't notice it in the first place. So, I guess I'm not sure if other people actually see it as abnormal or not.
Have other people told you that the part of your face you worry about looks normal or hardly noticeable?

Yeah, they have. That's actually a big part of why I came in to see you. Ever since I've had to be more in front of people at work for these events, I just... I can't stop staring at this one uneven-looking part of my face, especially in photos. But whenever I bring it up, everyone else says they barely see anything at all. They tell me it looks normal, but I just can't stop focusing on it.
Outside of worries about that part of your face, do you generally fear that other people will judge you negatively in social or work situations?

No, not really. I mean, I get normal nerves before a big event or a vendor meeting, just hoping everything runs smoothly. But I'm not really worried about people judging *me* as a person, or my personality or anything like that. It's really just... just the worry about my face. If it weren't for that, I think I'd be totally fine in those situations.
Are the mirror-checking and photo-retaking mainly because you feel that part of your face looks flawed?

Yeah, that's exactly why. Like, before I send out pictures from an event or right before I join a vendor meeting, I'll just keep checking my face in my phone camera. I end up retaking photos over and over, or I try to tilt my head a certain way so it doesn't look as bad. Sometimes I'll even ask a coworker if I look weird. It's all just because I'm so focused on how flawed it looks. And honestly, doing all of that can eat up enough time that I actually start falling behind on my planning stuff for work.
Do you think your worry about that part of your face is probably exaggerated compared with how it actually looks?

I mean... I don't really know. Everyone else tells me it's barely there, so I guess maybe they think I am. But when I look in the mirror or see myself in those event photos, it just looks so obvious to me. So, no, I don't feel like I'm exaggerating it. To me, it really does look exactly as bad as I think it does.
Is the main thing you keep getting stuck on that a part of your face looks defective or unattractive?

Yeah, that's the main thing. That's actually why I came in. Ever since I've had to be more out in front of people at work for events, I just... I can't stop staring at this one uneven-looking part of my face in all the photos. It just looks really unattractive and off to me, even when everyone else says they barely see anything at all.
